problems.source_says: The paper requests three solutions, rates all solutions, and specifies averaging across the two raters only. It never explicitly states how the solutions were combined within a participant or what one observation in the Table 2 Wilcoxon analysis represents. The within-person design makes participant a plausible unit, but does not establish that unit for these statistics. The form itself acknowledges the missing aggregation rule; under the required explicit-support standard, the unit remains unconfirmed for all three outcomes.
problems.quote: Final scores were averaged across the two raters.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (printed pp. 171-172), Measures: CPS performance; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 174), Data analysis; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 2. The complete markdown, including the Appendix, contains no further statement defining aggregation across solutions for these scores.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1, S1-O2 and S1-O3 are scores on produced solutions: two trained, condition-blinded raters independently rated all solutions from 1 (worst) to 5 (best), with randomized presentation and averaging across raters. This supports scored_on_output=true, human_raters, and criterion 3; expert credentials are not stated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Measures: CPS performance.

confirmed.statement: Originality is defined as novelty (S1-O1: novelty); quality as addressing task objectives (S1-O2: usefulness); elaboration as the level of detail (S1-O3: elaboration). None measures diversity across people or categories within a person.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Measures: CPS performance; codebook section 6, Construct.

confirmed.statement: All three outcomes were produced using the assigned GenAI tool in the same laboratory session. AI availability=yes, question=with_ai and timing=immediate are supported; neither condition removes AI before the scored task.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (printed pp. 171-172), Measures: CPS performance and Procedure; codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: Both conditions use GPT-4-based tools: standard ChatGPT-4 and personalised Mr. Ranedeer. Personalised versus standard is correctly coded ai_design.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), GenAI feedback conditions; codebook section 5.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 matches Table 2 exactly: Standard mean (SD) = 3.13 (1.27); Personalised mean (SD) = 2.92 (1.15); Wilcoxon z = -1.65; p = 0.098; Cohen’s r = -0.21; 95% CI for Cohen’s r = [-0.450, 0.044]. The no_clear_difference direction agrees with the reported test.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 2, Originality row and preceding Results paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 matches Table 2 exactly: Standard mean (SD) = 3.08 (1.12); Personalised mean (SD) = 3.50 (1.00); Wilcoxon z = -3.24; p = .001; Cohen’s r = -0.41; 95% CI for Cohen’s r = [-0.607, -0.166]. The treatment_higher direction agrees with the means and reported test.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 2, Quality row and preceding Results paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 matches Table 2 exactly: Standard mean (SD) = 2.48 (1.04); Personalised mean (SD) = 3.58 (1.17); Wilcoxon z = -6.25; p < .001; Cohen’s r = -0.79; 95% CI for Cohen’s r = [-0.885, -0.652]. The treatment_higher direction agrees with the means and reported test.

confirmed.statement: Table 2 gives no outcome-specific or condition-specific sample counts. The paper reports a final sample of 62 participants and a repeated-conditions design, but does not provide a count of scored observations for each Table 2 comparison.

summary: Output-based eligibility holds, and all three reported numerical results match Table 2. The participant analysis unit is not explicitly supported because aggregation across solutions is unspecified.
